paths.description: Public login entry and primary unauthenticated banking task; represents the only entry template.
Account recovery/new-user route linked from login; represents the secondary form flow.

findings.summary: The interface ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The light and dark screenshots are byte-identical (501,542 bytes), the computed color-scheme is normal, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, and browser-chrome colors.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no view-transition usage; the Angular recovery route replaces state without a declared transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion-safe same-document View Transition around route/state changes.

findings.summary: The cards adapt only through viewport breakpoints, not their containing context.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS contains multiple @media width rules but the probe found no @container/container-type usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable form-card containers container-type and move component-specific layout changes into @container rules with a fallback where needed.

findings.summary: Small link targets and absent input outline weaken touch and keyboard use.
findings.evidence: The probe measured recovery links at only 15px high and the focused input itself had outline:none and no box-shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44px effective touch targets and an unmistakable :focus-visible treatment on the whole input field.

findings.summary: The recovery/new-user route is served with an HTTP 404 and cannot be represented reliably as a successful navigation.
findings.evidence: The direct /gestion-usuario discoverability fetch returned 404 even though Angular later painted a form; both public recovery and registration links depend on this route.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve every application route with a successful document response and preserve a clear, distinct recovery/registration journey.

findings.summary: The login is materially slow on a mobile Lighthouse profile.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.5s, FCP 6.8s, Speed Index 7.8s and performance 0.52; the independent trace measured LCP 3.06s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the first useful login UI, reduce startup JavaScript, and verify LCP under representative mobile conditions.

findings.summary: Startup scripting exceeds the good responsiveness budget.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 258ms TBT; the trace also recorded a 51.27ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer nonessential startup work and split remaining long tasks into yieldable units.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and a slow dependency chain delay the login UI.
findings.evidence: HAR identified seven parser-inserted classic scripts without async/defer plus render-blocking CSS; trace FCP was 3.06s and Lighthouse FCP 6.8s.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer application scripts, remove body parser blockers, preload only the true critical resources, and self-host/optimize the critical font path.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 613KiB unused JavaScript: 446,638 bytes in main (72%); it also found 24KiB unused CSS (98%).
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split the old Angular bundle, remove unused chunks/polyfills, and load analytics and secondary code only when needed.

findings.summary: The visible brand logo has no text alternative.
findings.evidence: The images primitive and Lighthouse both found /assets/login/logo.png without alt; Lighthouse accessibility was 0.81.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise alt text if the logo conveys the product name, or alt="" if an equivalent adjacent accessible name is guaranteed.

findings.summary: The public views have no heading hierarchy and weak focus treatment.
findings.evidence: The DOM/evaluate probes found zero h1-h6 elements; the input’s focused outline and box-shadow were both none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real main landmark and descriptive h1 on each route, then provide visible :focus-visible styling that follows reading order.

findings.summary: Recovery and registration links have undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: At 360px the layout reflowed without overflow, but the two links measured only 15px high, well below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase link hit areas to at least 44 CSS px while retaining the successful mobile reflow.

findings.summary: A third-party monitoring request produces console and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded a CORS error and ERR_FAILED for https://bdv81mjs.staticmon.com/tun/bdv81mjs/input/.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the monitoring endpoint’s CORS contract or remove/contain the failing integration so login loads without console errors.

findings.summary: The logo asset lacks intrinsic dimensions and is much larger than displayed.
findings.evidence: The image is 1832px wide but displays at about 307px, has no width/height attributes, no srcset, and uses PNG.
findings.suggestedFix: Export a right-sized modern image, add width and height, and provide responsive sources when multiple display densities are required.

findings.summary: The page has no meta description.
findings.evidence: DOM and Lighthouse found a title but no meta[name=description].
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique Spanish description for the login/account service.

findings.summary: The site has no valid robots.txt.
findings.evidence: The explicit /robots.txt fetch returned HTTP 404 with the app shell body. Links and viewport metadata otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid text/plain robots.txt and make its policy explicit.

findings.summary: Indexing signals conflict with application routing.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returned 404, no canonical or hreflang was present, and direct /gestion-usuario returned HTTP 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct 2xx statuses for public routes, add canonical URLs, and provide a sitemap consistent with robots policy.

findings.summary: The branded public service has no social-preview or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The probe found no Open Graph tags and no JSON-LD despite visible BDVenlínea product branding.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and minimal Organization/WebApplication JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: A banking login omits core security headers and sets insecure cookies.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but headers found no CSP, HSTS or nosniff; cookies found five cookies without Secure and every observed cookie had SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is strictly required.

findings.summary: The login sends data to a broad tracking and monitoring footprint before authentication.
findings.evidence: Trackers found 10 third-party origins and three known trackers; HAR recorded 16 third-party requests and 352,659 transferred bytes, including DoubleClick and Google audiences.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove nonessential advertising/tracking from the banking login, minimize events, and load strictly necessary analytics only under a documented privacy basis.

findings.summary: The authentication entry shows no phishing-resistant sign-in option.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse confirmed no permission prompts on load, but the login exposes only a username-first flow and the probe found no WebAuthn/credential capability use.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey/WebAuthn authentication and retain a well-protected recovery fallback.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are absent on a high-risk authentication origin.
findings.evidence: Headers found no HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, a strict Referrer-Policy, a minimal Permissions-Policy, and Trusted Types where the Angular app can support it.

findings.summary: Core login and recovery content disappear without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 0% raw-to-rendered content coverage; crawler screenshots show a blank page while the browser screenshots contain both forms.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the essential form purpose, labels and recovery links, then hydrate/enhance behavior client-side.

findings.summary: The installable shell does not show evidence of a cached offline application fallback.
findings.evidence: A valid manifest and active ngsw-worker exist, but CacheStorage showed the application-shell cache empty; only three favicon/isologo assets were cached.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure the service worker to cache a safe unauthenticated shell and explicit offline/retry view without caching sensitive account data.

findings.summary: HTTP route failure is masked by a rendered form rather than handled intentionally.
findings.evidence: A direct fetch of /gestion-usuario returned 404 while JavaScript rendered the management form; no route error or recovery explanation was shown.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix route status handling and present explicit retry/back recovery for genuine HTTP/network failures.

findings.summary: The management form shows an error before the user interacts.
findings.evidence: The first screenshot of /gestion-usuario already displays “Complete la cédula, sin caracteres especiales” while the field is untouched and empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay validation until blur or submit and announce the resulting error accessibly.

findings.summary: The username field explicitly disables autofill.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reported autocomplete="off" on the username input.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the correct autocomplete="username" token and appropriate current-password/webauthn tokens in subsequent authentication steps.

findings.summary: Account entry/recovery lacks modern reauthentication and clear differentiated entry points.
findings.evidence: The public UI exposes username-first authentication only; both “forgot” and “new client” links use /gestion-usuario, and no passkey capability was detected.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate and label recovery/registration outcomes, add phishing-resistant authentication and require proportionate reauthentication for sensitive changes.

findings.summary: The login logo is oversized and not responsively encoded.
findings.evidence: The logo’s natural width is 1832px versus a 307px display width, with PNG, no srcset and no intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate right-sized WebP/AVIF variants and responsive source selection while preserving the existing WebP background.

findings.summary: The tiny login performs disproportionate background and startup work.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 1.18MB across 37 requests; Lighthouse estimated 613KiB unused JS, while analytics/monitoring requests fire before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate unused bundles and defer or batch nonessential analytics/monitoring until after consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Third-party code consumes a large share of the login budget.
findings.evidence: Sixteen third-party requests transferred 352,659 bytes; GTM/gtag alone transferred about 285KiB and known trackers included Analytics and DoubleClick.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget, remove advertising endpoints, and defer any retained analytics.
